summary.title: LF git repositories (rt-tests, kernel.org)
summary.one_liner: The page is an Anubis bot-protection interstitial on git.kernel.org, not the rt-tests content, so it teaches nothing about the tool itself.
takeaways: The fetched page is an Anubis proof-of-work challenge page, not the rt-tests repository contents.
Anubis uses a Hashcash-style proof-of-work scheme to make mass scraping more expensive.
Anubis requires modern JavaScript, so plugins such as JShelter may need to be disabled for the domain.
The rt-tests repository details (README, wakeup-latency measurement) could not be verified from this page.
summary.summary: The page at git.kernel.org for the rt-tests repository only shows an Anubis anti-bot interstitial. It explains that Anubis runs a Hashcash-style proof-of-work check to slow down AI scrapers and that it needs modern JavaScript, so plugins like JShelter must be disabled for the domain. No rt-tests code, README, or latency methodology appears in the text. The listing notes rt-tests as the reference wakeup-latency tool for Linux, but that claim is not confirmed by this page.
